title: Modular Optical Ptychography through Differentiable Programming
content: Phase imaging is crucial in optical microscopy because phase shifts are often more sensitive indicators of a specimen’s subtle features than intensity variations [1]. A single recorded image, however, does not independently reveal both phase and amplitude, prompting a variety of strategies to overcome this limitation. Approaches such as phase-plate microscopy [2] and holography [3] have found widespread application, but each method introduces its own hardware requirements and trade-offs. Among computational solutions, ptychography [4] stands out for its ability to retrieve quantitative phase information while simultaneously disentangling the microscope’s optical transfer function from the sample itself—a capability that enhances overall imaging fidelity in diverse optical configurations.
